account_bind_web.help:
## Information

Linking your account to an e-mail address allows you to play the browser version of Tetrarchy Falls using this account.

We will send you a confirmation e-mail with next steps.

account_delete.explain_1: Deleting your account is permanent. Your login, email address and personal data are removed. Your game history stays, under an anonymous name that is not linked to you.
account_delete.explain_2: To start, enter your password. We will send a confirmation link to your email address. The link expires in 1 hour.
account_delete.explain_3: After you confirm, your account is locked for 14 days and then permanently deleted. You can log back in during those 14 days to cancel.
account_delete.sent: Confirmation email sent. Check your inbox and follow the link to confirm the deletion.

account_link_discord.expires_in: This code expires in {minutes} minutes. Generate a new one if you don't get to it in time.
account_link_discord.instructions: In Discord, run `/link code:{code}` in any channel where **Marat** is present (or in a DM). Marat will confirm with an ephemeral reply only you can see.
account_link_discord.intro: Link your Discord account so Marat — the Tetrarchy Falls bot — can recognize you in our community and game servers. Once linked, Marat can assign you to faction chats, DM you when important things happen in-game, and answer slash-command queries about your fleets and agents.
account_link_discord.show_profile_hint: Lets anyone use the /player command on Discord to see a snapshot of your game stats (wins, daily medals, factions played). Never shows personal info like your email.
account_link_discord.timezone_role_hint: Adds a role tag like “TZ: Europe/Paris” to your linked Discord account so other players know when you are around. The role is created automatically if needed.
account_link_discord.timezone_role_label: Show my timezone as a Discord role
account_link_discord.unlink_note: To unlink, run `/unlink` in Discord. The bot will ask you to confirm.

account_locked.days_left: Your account will be permanently deleted in {days} day(s).
account_locked.explain_locked: While your account is being deleted, it can not do anything until it is permanently deleted, or you cancel the deletion. Games, maps and all other features are locked.
account_locked.explain_policy: When the deletion completes, your login, email address and personal data are removed. Your game history stays under an anonymous name that is not linked to you. Backup copies expire within 30 days.

maps.no_results: No results found yet — click New map above to design one.
maps.about_body: A map is just the layout — star systems, sectors, blackholes. It doesn't have factions or victory conditions on its own. Once a map exists, you (or anyone else) can build a scenario from it that turns it into a playable game.
maps.roadmap_body: Symmetric (mirrored) map layouts, shape primitives instead of triangle grouping, and per-sector system counts are next on the redesign roadmap.

scenarios.no_results: No results found yet — open a map and click Use for a scenario to build one.
scenarios.about_body: A scenario is a playable game derived from a map: factions, victory points per sector, starting year, time limit and speed. Players join an instance spun from a scenario; the underlying map can be reused across many scenarios.
scenarios.roadmap_body: More gameplay mutators, per-scenario victory stats, and per-sector neutral distribution controls are next on the redesign roadmap.

step_descriptions.0: Pick the overall scale of the playable area. Bigger maps fit more sectors and more players but take longer to traverse and to play out.
step_descriptions.1: A random Voronoi grid is generated — these triangles are raw tiles you will later group into sectors. Tweak the seed for a fresh layout, or the triangle size to make tiles bigger or smaller. You can also skip past this step entirely if you plan to draw sectors with shape primitives.
step_descriptions.2: Build named sectors. Choose Voronoi triangles to paint sectors by grouping the underlying tiles, or shape primitives to draw rectangles, ellipses, and regular polygons directly. You can mix both within one map. You need at least two sectors.
step_descriptions.3: Star systems are placed probabilistically inside each sector. The density and grouping sliders control how clustered or spread out the systems are. Re-roll the seed to see different placements; the controls take effect when you release the slider.
step_descriptions.4: Optional final touches: carve out blackhole exclusion zones (no systems can sit inside, and ships route around them), or use the removal tool to delete unwanted systems inside a circle.
step_descriptions.5: Give the map a name and a short description so other authors can recognize it in the list. Save when ready — the map becomes available as a base for scenarios.

map_editor.show_grid_tooltip: Overlay a grid the size of the maximum ship jump distance — useful for seeing how reachable systems are from each other.
map_editor.show_max_bond_distance_tooltip: Show a circle around the mouse with radius equal to the maximum jump distance. Systems falling inside this circle of each other will be auto-connected.
map_editor.sector_info_tooltip: Show each sector's name and its system count on top of the map.
map_editor.show_connections_tooltip: Preview the warp lanes that will be auto-computed between systems based on proximity. Blackholes break lanes that would pass through them. System dots are always rendered separately — this toggle only controls the connection lines, and turning it off also skips fetching the preview from the server (useful for large maps).
map_editor.edges_intersector_only_tooltip: Show only warp lanes that cross a sector boundary. The intra-sector mesh can be too dense to read at a glance on large maps; this view emphasizes how sectors connect to each other instead.
map_editor.info_grid_radius: The size of the grid and the radius of the circle around the mouse correspond to the maximum jump distance.
map_editor.triangles_size_tooltip: Controls the size of the raw triangle tiles you will group into sectors at the next step. Smaller triangles give you finer control over sector shapes; larger ones are faster to assemble.
map_editor.info_ctrl_triangles: Hold down the CTRL key and hover the cursor over the triangles to pair them in a row.
map_editor.mode_triangles_desc: Group the underlying tiles into sectors. Best for organic, irregular shapes.
map_editor.mode_shapes_desc: Draw rectangles, ellipses, and regular polygons directly. Best for symmetric or geometric layouts.
map_editor.shape_select_sector_first: Pick a sector from the list before drawing.
map_editor.shape_pick_tool: Pick a tool: Select to move and rotate placed shapes, Rectangle for two-click axis-aligned rectangles, or Polygon for free-form polygons.
map_editor.shape_first_click_hint: Click on the map to place the first corner of the rectangle.
map_editor.shape_draft_hint: Click again to commit the rectangle, or press Esc to cancel.
map_editor.polygon_first_click_hint: Click to place the first vertex. Each click adds a vertex; snap is on by default so clicks near existing edges or vertices pull into alignment.
map_editor.polygon_continue_hint: Click to add another vertex. Snap pulls the cursor toward nearby edges and vertices.
map_editor.polygon_close_hint: Click the first vertex (green) to close, press Enter to close to the start vertex, or Esc to cancel.
map_editor.polygon_close_now_hint: Click to close this polygon. When start and last are on the same sector, the shared border is stitched automatically along the shorter perimeter direction.
map_editor.symmetry_hint: Draw your sectors in the clear quadrant. The cross-hatched area is the mirror region — vertex placement is blocked there and the mirror is generated automatically at step 3. Vertices placed within the snap radius of the axis pull onto it so sectors meet exactly at the shared border.
map_editor.debug_export_tooltip: Download the current sector + system data as a JSON file (also copies to clipboard and logs to console). Useful for sharing weird-looking merges or path-traces with whoever maintains the editor.
map_editor.debug_export_done: Debug data downloaded and copied to clipboard.
map_editor.tests_run_tooltip: Run the polygon-merge regression test cases. Results print to the browser console. Useful after editing the merge tier or the snap pipeline.
map_editor.tests_fail: Editor tests: {passed}/{total} passed — see console for failures.
map_editor.shape_select_hint: Click a shape to select it. Drag to move; drag the handle above the shape to rotate; press Delete to remove. Sectors can have multiple shapes — drawing always adds to the active sector.
map_editor.snap_enabled_tooltip: When dragging or drawing, pull the shape toward the edge of any other shape within the snap radius. Off = free placement, no auto-alignment.
map_editor.overlap_warning: {count} sectors overlap each other. Overlap is allowed but may produce unpredictable system placement and faction starts.
map_editor.sector_overlap_tooltip: This sector overlaps another. Overlap is allowed, but planet placement and faction starts may behave unpredictably where polygons cross.
map_editor.toast_sector_pieces_dropped: {name}: some parts of the sector were dropped (the shapes didn't merge into one connected polygon).
map_editor.overall_density_tooltip: Roughly how many systems to place per unit of sector area, before any grouping. Higher density = more systems overall.
map_editor.group_density_tooltip: How tightly packed each group of systems is. High density = a tight cluster; low density = systems trickle out toward the group's edges.
map_editor.group_count_tooltip: How many clusters of systems to generate per sector. With 1, every sector forms a single blob; with several, sectors look like multiple linked star clusters.
map_editor.group_spread_tooltip: How far the groups themselves are pushed apart inside the sector. Low spread = groups overlap into one mass; high spread = each group has its own corner.
map_editor.group_attenuation_tooltip: How sharply system density falls off as you move away from each group's center. High attenuation = tight cores with empty space between groups; low attenuation = a softer, more diffuse galaxy.
map_editor.per_sector_count_description: Pin an exact number of systems for any sector. The hot-point falloff above still shapes where they land — leave a sector blank to use the global density.
map_editor.sector_system_count_tooltip: Place exactly this many systems in this sector. Leave blank to let the global density decide.
map_editor.system_removal_tool_tooltip: Switch the cursor to a deletion circle: clicking on the map removes every system that falls inside the circle. Useful for carving out empty corridors after generation.
map_editor.blackhole_creation_tool_tooltip: Switch the cursor to a blackhole placer. Clicking the map drops a blackhole of the chosen radius and erases any systems too close to it. Warp lanes can never pass through a blackhole.
map_editor.deletion_circle_size_tooltip: Radius of the cursor circle used by the removal tool. Bigger circle = wipes more systems per click.
map_editor.blackhole_size_tooltip: Radius of the blackhole exclusion zone. Larger blackholes erase more systems on placement and force warp lanes to take longer detours around them.
map_editor.toast_empty_sector: Every sector needs at least one system. Increase the density or re-roll the seed.

step_descriptions.0: Set the high-level rules of the game: how fast time passes, the starting year, the random seed, and the galaxy-wide neutral distribution.
step_descriptions.1: Assign each sector on the map to a faction. Click a faction in the list, then click sectors on the map to claim them. At least two factions need at least one sector each; unassigned sectors stay neutral; factions with no sectors are dropped.
step_descriptions.2: Set how the game ends: pick a maximum duration, and assign victory points to each sector. The first faction to control sectors totaling the victory threshold wins. Sectors with more points are more strategically valuable. You can also pin the conquest milestones to exact point totals instead of the automatic formula.
step_descriptions.3: Final summary — verify the scenario settings and save. The scenario will appear in the scenarios list and become joinable as a game.

scenario_editor.scenario_speed_tooltip: Sets the real-time pace of the game. Fast = a session lasts hours; Medium = days; Slow = a weeks-long campaign. Affects every per-time rate (production, research, etc.).
scenario_editor.scenario_mode_tooltip: Production runs the normal game rules. Development is for testing — it relaxes some balance constraints and shouldn't be used for real matches.
scenario_editor.starting_year_tooltip: In-game year the campaign starts in. Purely flavor — affects displayed dates but not mechanics.
scenario_editor.factions_info_minimum: At least 2 factions with at least one sector are required.
scenario_editor.factions_info_no_sector_removed: Factions without sectors are removed from the scenario.
scenario_editor.mutators_info: Pick any number of optional gameplay changes. If none selected then vanilla rules apply.
scenario_editor.neutral_info: How many habitable systems start as neutral.
scenario_editor.neutral_mode_rng_desc: Each habitable system rolls for neutral control chance against the Speed's built-in RNG threshold.
scenario_editor.neutral_mode_fixed_desc: Each sector gets the same percent of habitable planets under neutral control, no RNG.
scenario_editor.sector_neutral_tooltip: How this sector picks neutrals. Default inherits the scenario-wide setting; Override RNG forces per-system rolls at the chosen ratio; Override Fixed pins exactly floor(N × ratio) neutrals. The preview shows the resulting count.
scenario_editor.max_duration_tooltip: Hard cap on game length. When time runs out, whichever faction has the most victory-point-weighted sector control wins. Allowed range depends on the chosen speed.
scenario_editor.conquest_info: The conquest victory track pays 2 / 5 / 10 victory points for holding sectors worth each milestone's point total. By default the game computes the milestones from the map's total points, faction count and player balance; set them by hand to make sector values read as exact targets.
scenario_editor.conquest_total_tooltip: Sum of the victory points currently assigned to all sectors below — the pool the conquest milestones are measured against.
scenario_editor.conquest_mode_auto_desc: The engine derives the three milestones from total sector points, the number of factions, and each faction's player count at game time.
scenario_editor.conquest_mode_custom_desc: Pin the three milestones to exact point totals. Every faction chases the same numbers, regardless of player counts.
scenario_editor.conquest_preview_tooltip: What the formula gives with evenly-filled factions. Uneven player counts shift each faction's milestones up or down by up to ±50% in game.
scenario_editor.conquest_invalid: Milestones must be whole numbers, at least 1, in ascending order.
scenario_editor.conquest_unreachable: The last milestone is above the total sector points — no faction will be able to reach it.
scenario_editor.victory_points_tooltip: Points this sector is worth toward a victory. Set higher on chokepoints and contested cores, lower on peripheral or starter sectors.
scenario_editor.game_mode_tooltip: Standard: player factions fight each other. Rebel Defense: every player joins one faction against the Rebellion, which the game commands.

invites.title: Invite a player
invites.description:
## Invite-only

Tetrarchy Falls accounts are invite-only. Generate a 24-hour link below and send it to whomever you'd like to invite. Any number of people can sign up with the same link until it expires.

Generating a fresh link each time is fine — there's no limit. Old links keep working until they expire on their own.
invites.generated_no_copy: Link generated — copy it manually below
invites.error_disabled: Your account is not allowed to generate invite links. Contact an administrator if you think this is a mistake.
invites.error_rate_limited: You're generating links too quickly. Try again in a little while.
invites.error_generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.

menu.ea_p1: Tetrarchy Falls is in early access, joining us on Discord is the best way of finding players.
menu.ea_p2: A good portion of the game is translated into English, but don't hesitate to ask questions directly in game or on Discord if some things are not clear.
menu.ea_p3: Every Monday, end of the day, we release a new version of the game with new features and patches. Detailed information about these updates is available on Discord.
menu.epic_p1: Every Tuesday evening at 8:45pm UTC+1 there is an official Flash game with rewards.
menu.epic_p2: Flash matches are only available to players who own the full version of the game.
menu.legacy_p1: A Legacy game (about 30 days) will start Wednesday 14th of July 2021, 8pm CEST. We’re still improving this mode and this test is intended to improve game elements balance and calibration.
menu.tactical_p1: Every Wednesday evening at 8pm UTC+1 an official TACTIC game is launched for a duration of 5 days.
menu.web_p1: Play Tetrarchy Falls in your browser by getting to the “Settings” (top right of the screen once you’ve clicked on “Play”) and link your email address, you will then be able to connect to our web portal.
menu.web_p2: Please note that for now Chrome (and Chrome-based browsers) is the only fully supported browser.

upgrade.steam_id_info:
## Help

Getting your Steam ID will allow us to link your account with the Steam version of the game. Once the upgrade completed, you will receive a Steam key that will allow you to activate your product and play both the browser and Steam versions with the same account.

To find your Steam ID, go to this web address [store.steampowered.com/account](https://store.steampowered.com/account/) and log in. Your Steam ID is located at the top of the page, below your account name, as shown in the image below. Put only the number in the text field.

![steam help](media/steam-id-help.png)

scenario_workshop.load_failed: The workshop couldn't load. Try again in a moment.
scenario_workshop.copied: The scenario is on your clipboard.
scenario_workshop.syntax_banner: Line {line}: {message}. The nodes show the last version that read correctly.
scenario_workshop.fix_syntax_first: Fix the error in the text first; the nodes need a script that reads correctly.
scenario_workshop.help_intro: A scenario is a challenge you design: what the world looks like (setup), how players are ranked (score) and what happens while they play (events). The nodes and the code are two views of the same scenario; change either and the other follows.
scenario_workshop.help_wires: The thick white wires set the order things happen in, top to bottom. Drag from a node’s bottom pin to another node to put it next.
scenario_workshop.help_values: The thin wires carry values into a node’s left side. Plain values (numbers, text, choices) are typed straight into the node. Durations read like 15s or 2m, percentages like 25%.
scenario_workshop.help_code: Right-click a step or a value and choose “Show as code” to write that part as text, without leaving the nodes; ⤢ turns a line of code back into nodes. Lambdas such as s => s.population always show as code.
scenario_workshop.help_group: Select a run of steps in one chain (shift-click them, or shift-drag a box around them), then press Ctrl+G to turn them into a function you can name, reuse and save to your library. Selecting an if or a loop takes its inner steps along.
scenario_workshop.help_keys: Drag the background to pan, scroll to zoom, double-click to add a node, Delete to remove, Alt-click a pin to disconnect it. In the node list on the left, click a name for its docs and double-click it to add it.
scenario_workshop.wire_mismatch: Those two pins don’t fit: order wires join order pins, value wires join value pins.
scenario_workshop.bad_path: A path is names joined by dots, such as player.income.credit.
scenario_workshop.bad_name: A name is letters, digits and _, and can’t start with a digit.
scenario_workshop.pin_exec_in: Runs after the node wired here
scenario_workshop.pin_exec_out: Drag to the node that runs next
scenario_workshop.pin_data_out: Drag to the input that uses this value
scenario_workshop.code_hint: Written as code. Right-click the node to show it as nodes.
scenario_workshop.sim_quiet: Nothing happened: no event fired, no action ran.
scenario_workshop.pretend_hint: The model player never researches patents, builds fleets or removes agents on its own. To test a goal like that, add a what-if: from the time you give, the simulator reads your value instead. It starts from what your when conditions read.
scenario_workshop.sim_model: The simulator plays a model player who starts with {start} credits and whose income per game day rises over the run: credits {c0} to {c1}, technology {t0} to {t1}, ideology {i0} to {i1}. A game day passes every 0.75 seconds, so a 20-minute run is 1,600 game days. Your actions come on top. It shows what your scenario does and when; it isn’t a real game.

palette.doc_on_start: Runs once, as the run begins.
palette.doc_on_end: Runs once when the run ends, after the score is counted.
palette.doc_every: Runs again and again on a schedule. “count as” numbers the runs 1, 2, 3 …
palette.doc_at: Runs once, when the clock reaches the time.
palette.doc_when: Runs each time its condition turns true (checked every second).
palette.doc_score: How players are ranked: a number, counted when the run ends. Higher is better. For a race, use time.left and call finish() at the goal.
palette.doc_tiebreak: Ranks players with the same score. Higher is better.
palette.doc_var: A value the scenario remembers between events, such as a counter or the next tithe.
palette.doc_fn: A function: a named group of steps you can call from anywhere and reuse.
palette.doc_setup: What the world looks like: the name, the time limit, the sector, a rival court, mutators, patents.
palette.doc_if: Choose a path: true runs one chain, false the other, then the flow continues below.
palette.doc_for: Run a chain once for each item of a list.
palette.doc_while: Run a chain again and again while a condition holds.
palette.doc_let: Name a value for the steps that follow.
palette.doc_assign: Change a variable (a var, or one made with let).
palette.doc_return: End a function and hand back a value.
palette.doc_note: A note for whoever reads the scenario. It does nothing.
palette.doc_cond: A value that depends on a condition: if a then b else c.

tour.label: Workshop tour
tour.task_todo: Try it now, or skip this step.
tour.welcome_body: A scenario is a challenge you design, like a daily. Read it top to bottom: the setup, how players are ranked, then what happens while they play. Drag the background to look around.
tour.events_body: An event node starts a chain of steps: on start runs once, every 2m runs every two minutes. The thick white wires show the order the steps run in.
tour.values_body: The give node hands the player credits. The amount is worked out just above it, in the * node: 500 times the gift count. Click the 500, change it to 1000 and press Enter. The message below uses the same amount.
tour.add_body: Drag notify from the Actions list onto the canvas, then drag from the bottom pin of a node in a chain to it. Or drop it straight onto that pin.
tour.simulate_body: Simulate plays the whole run against a model player in a second and lists what your scenario did, and when.
tour.code_body: Prefer typing? Switch to Code or Both. It’s the same scenario as text: edit either side and the other follows.
tour.done_body: Open the examples for the dailies rebuilt as scenarios. Help (on the right) has the shortcuts; the tour button brings this back.

scenario_workshop.playtest_hint: Play your scenario in a real game. Your script runs it; messages and errors show at the top of the screen.
scenario_workshop.playtest_errors: Fix the errors first: a scenario with errors can't be played.
scenario_workshop.switched: Opened {name}. Undo (Ctrl+Z) brings your last scenario back.
scenario_workshop.stale: Out of date: the scenario changed since this run.
scenario_workshop.grouped: Grouped into {name}(). Its framed box is below the rest; Fit shows everything.
scenario_workshop.library_replace: Replace the saved {name} with this version?
scenario_workshop.sim_no_finish: finish() never ran: the goal wasn’t reached in this run. Try a stronger economy or a longer time limit, or test the finish with a what-if.
scenario_workshop.opened: Opened {name}. Undo brings back what you had.
scenario_workshop.file_too_big: That file is too big for a script (64 KB at most).
scenario_workshop.drop_here: Drop an .edict file to open it
scenario_workshop.link_hint: The workshop follows {name}: save it in your editor and it reloads here. Save (Ctrl+S) writes changes made here back to it.
scenario_workshop.linked: Following {name}. Save it in your editor and the workshop updates; Ctrl+S here saves back to it.
scenario_workshop.link_conflict: {name} changed on disk, and the workshop has changes not saved to it. Load the file and drop the changes made here?
scenario_workshop.link_lost: Can’t reach {name} any more (moved, deleted, or permission withdrawn). Stopped following it.
scenario_workshop.link_denied: The browser wasn’t allowed to write to {name}. Nothing was saved.
scenario_workshop.export_header: Functions from my Scenario Workshop library, exported {day}.
scenario_workshop.import_replace: Your library already has different functions named {names}. Replace them?
scenario_workshop.import_done_partial: Added to your library from {name}: {count}. Only functions are imported; the file’s other parts were left out.
scenario_workshop.editors_intro: Prefer VS Code, a JetBrains IDE or Notepad++? These add Edict to them: highlighting, completion, docs on hover and parameter hints, from the game’s own list of what scripts can use. Instructions are inside.
scenario_workshop.editors_link: Then, in File, choose Link a file: the workshop follows the file as you save it in your editor, with its nodes, problems and simulation.
scenario_workshop.editors_open: Then open the file here (File > Open file, or drop it on the page) to see its nodes, problems and simulation. In Chrome or Edge, the workshop can also follow a file as you save it.
scenario_workshop.server_busy: The server is still working on your last few requests. Try again in a moment.
scenario_workshop.server_too_many: That’s a lot of requests in a few minutes. Wait a minute, then try again.
scenario_workshop.deleted_with_steps: Deleted {what} and the step in it. | Deleted {what} and the {count} steps in it.
scenario_workshop.suggest_hint: {key} to insert · ↑↓ to choose · Esc to close
scenario_workshop.doc_unknown: {name} isn’t something the game knows, so there are no docs for it. Check the spelling; the problem below may name the right one.
scenario_workshop.doc_more: More in the Help tab: double-click the node.
scenario_workshop.doc_fn_plain: A function in this script. A comment on the line above its fn becomes this description.
scenario_workshop.doc_empty: Click a node or a name in the code to see its docs here, or pick one from the reference below. Double-click a node to jump here.
scenario_workshop.reference_hint: Click a name to see its docs at the top.
scenario_workshop.palette_add_hint: Click for its docs; double-click, drag or press Enter to add it.
scenario_workshop.doc_lib_details: Adding it copies the function into your scenario, where you can change it; the library keeps its own copy.
